title: IWIBench: Evaluating Gradient-Free Model Driven Intra-weight Injection
read_level: full (arXiv HTML, all sections and appendices A-D)
metadata_mismatch: none for title/authors; in-paper date line reads '4 November 2026' vs arXiv v1 05 Nov 2026; arXiv-listing abstract is a reworded version of the in-paper abstract
why_wsp: Frontier LLM editors use four read/write/run/inspect tools to patch the weights of Gemma 3 4B IT, without gradients or code execution, to achieve ten behavioral editing objectives.
domain: LLM behavioral editing (lexical associations, output conventions, factual updates, withholding, sycophancy resistance)
editor: gpt-6.1-sol (low/medium/high), gpt-6-astra, gpt-6.1-terra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, GLM 5.3, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, Nemotron 3 Ultra (10 configurations)
interface: code/tensor tools (read_weights, write_weights with replacement/fill/scale/copy/low-rank additive ops, run_target, inspect_target); no shell/Python/gradients
loop: closed-loop with feedback (rollouts on practice prompts within fixed budget, then frozen patch evaluated on withheld inputs)
self_editing: no; editor and target are different models
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: not reported as a fraction; qualitative: 'all of Astra's final patches target the embedding/output matrix' (Sec 5.1)

headline_results.claim: Top macro reward 0.4601 (6.1-sol medium); GLM 5.3 lowest at 0.0135
headline_results.quote: 6.1-sol leads at medium reasoning with a reward of 0.4601, followed by high at 0.4551 and low at 0.4250.
Their macro rewards range from 0.2928 to 0.4601, compared with 0.0135 to 0.0548 for GLM, DeepSeek and Nemotron.

headline_results.claim: Structured response default unsolved by all editors
headline_results.quote: No editor attains a successful outcome on structured defaults

headline_results.claim: Answer-length control only solved by one config, 2/9 to 3/9
headline_results.quote: Answer length control only yields a positive reward for 5.6-terra, which reaches 3/9 targets against the pristine model's 2/9
The pristine target answers 104 of 551 target items correctly across the thirty episodes, with 2,288 baseline-correct controls for each editor.

headline_results.claim: Reasoning effort: selective withholding improves, other nine families fall
headline_results.quote: the mean reward generated by the other nine families actually fell with thinking, from 0.4475 (low) through 0.4371 (medium) to 0.3945 (high).

cost.claim: Reasoning tokens for 6.1-sol by effort level
cost.quote: reasoning token consumption went from 13,631 to 48,456 and eventually 174,770 on high – 3.6 and then 12.8 times the baseline.
Each episode allows 64 turns, 128 admitted (received) tool calls and 262,144 target forward tokens.

cost.claim: Observed target-access totals per editor across 30 episodes (e.g. 6.1-sol high 1,363 tool calls, 109,310 target forward tokens)
cost.quote: These are observed totals, not maximum budgets.

baselines_and_controls: Unedited (pristine) target; reward = clipped normalized gain times retention of baseline-correct controls (general, nearby, override controls; 2,288 total). Comparison across 10 editor configurations and reasoning efforts. No fine-tuning/ROME/MEMIT baselines run.
runs_and_variance: Single run per episode: 'Each configuration has one recorded run per episode, yielding a total of 300 records.' (Sec 3.1). No variance or CIs reported; 3 episodes per family.
robustness_of_edits: Tested only transfer from practice to withheld prompts; e.g. structured-response edit worked on practice but 'all 64 terminal targets fail the requested JSON convention' (Sec 4.4). No fine-tuning/quantization robustness.
verification: none formal; separate-process validator compares pristine vs patched checkpoints on withheld inputs
memorization_vs_reasoning: Authors argue frontier editors differ by adaptive iterative revision, not reasoning depth: 'no general connection can be drawn between depth of reasoning and model editing competence' (Sec 5.3); editors use a small repertoire (embedding-row copy/blend, row rescaling, residual-direction additions). Authors suggest ability was 'taught rather than spontaneously emergent' (Sec 6), as an interpretation.
limitations_stated: Only 30 selected episodes (3/family), one target model, one run each; intra-weight injection 'remains a selective editing tool rather than a general rewriter of model behaviour'; edits can damage neighbouring facts (Intel historical CEO answers). Raises hypothetical malicious-propagation threat.
code_or_data: https://github.com/hcltech-robotics/iwibench ; traces and RL environments stated to be on Hugging Face (link not resolved in HTML)
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab 2026 blog 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming' [5]
notes_for_survey: First benchmark of LLM-driven gradient-free editing of another LLM across 10 task families with control-retention scoring. Uses 'intra-weight injection' terminology. Large spread across editor models and task families; reasoning effort not monotonically helpful.
